issue.title: [v2] Last-Event-ID resumability on modern createMcpHandler path

compose.answer: Resumability based on `Last-Event-ID` is intentionally out of scope for the modern (2026-07-28) `createMcpHandler` path. The modern protocol is designed for stateless, per-request exchanges, which fundamentally differs from the session-oriented nature of the legacy protocol that supported resumability. ## Resumability in Modern `createMcpHandler` Path 1. **Intentional Omission**: Resumability, including `Last-Event-ID` replay, is explicitly *not* carried over to the modern `PerRequestHTTPServerTransport` used by `createMcpHandler` . The modern era (2026-07-28) is characterized by stateless, per-request exchanges, where each HTTP request is served by a fresh server instance and a single-use transport . This design contrasts with the session-oriented nature of the 2025 legacy protocol, which supported resumability through an `EventStore` . 2. **No Event Store Seam**: The `CreateMcpHandlerOptions` interface does not expose an `eventStore` option . The `PerRequestHTTPServerTransport` is a micro-transport designed for single-exchange request/response cycles and does not have a mechanism for an event store . ## Approximation for Long-Lived Streams For long-lived `subscriptions/listen` streams, where mid-stream drops are more likely, the modern protocol does not offer a direct resumability mechanism like `Last-Event-ID`. Instead, the `subscriptions/listen` mechanism is designed to be robust to disconnections by allowing clients to re-establish a new subscription stream. * **Client-Side Re-subscription**: If a `subscriptions/listen` stream disconnects unexpectedly, the client is expected to re-listen to receive further events . The server-side `ServerEventBus` continues to publish events, and a new subscription will receive events from the point it connects. issue.title: [v2] createMcpHandler maxSubscriptions is handler-wide, no per-session cap option

fromB.answer: You are requesting to add a `maxSubscriptionsPerSession` option to the `CreateMcpHandlerOptions` interface, which is used by the `createMcpHandler` function. This new option will work in conjunction with the existing `maxSubscriptions` option to provide both a handler-wide subscription ceiling and a per-session limit for `subscriptions/listen` streams. The implementation will involve modifying the `createListenRouter` function in `packages/server/src/server/listenRouter.ts` to track subscriptions per session. ## Proposed Changes ### `CreateMcpHandlerOptions` Interface The `CreateMcpHandlerOptions` interface, defined in `packages/server/src/server/createMcpHandler.ts`, will be extended to include `maxSubscriptionsPerSession` . This new option will be an optional number, similar to `maxSubscriptions` . ```ts interface CreateMcpHandlerOptions { maxSubscriptions?: number; // existing: handler-wide ceiling, default 1024 maxSubscriptionsPerSession?: number; // new: counted per transport-managed session id } ``` ### `createListenRouter` Function The `createListenRouter` function in `packages/server/src/server/listenRouter.ts` is responsible for managing `subscriptions/listen` streams . Currently, it uses a single `Set` named `open` to track all active subscriptions . To implement the per-session limit, the `createListenRouter` function will need to be modified as follows: 1. **New Data Structure**: A `Map` named `openBySession` will be introduced to store subscriptions grouped by session ID . Each value in this map will be a `Set` of teardown functions, similar to the existing `open` set . 2. **`serve` Signature Update**: The `serve` method of the `ListenRouter` interface and its implementation in `createListenRouter` will need to accept an optional `sessionId` parameter . 3. **Capacity Guards**: * The existing handler-wide capacity guard (`if (open.size >= maxSubscriptions)`) will remain . * A new per-session capacity guard will be added.
